title: Stage-handoff reservoir policy for latency/fairness balancing in prefill->decode
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce a ‘reservoir’ based handoff policy at the prefill->decode boundary to reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants while preserving aggregate throughput and fairness. The reservoir behaves like a per-tenant, time-decayed credit pool used by the stage-handoff arbiter to decide whether to: fast-track the decode (allocate low-latency slots), split the prefill into micro-slices, or defer until a lower-cost kernel path is available.
background: Current prefill->decode arbitration uses coarse priority buckets and temporal slices which can either favor throughput (large contiguous slices) or latency (small slices with hedging). We've observed long-tail 95/99p latency regressions for enterprise tenants under mixed workloads where long prefill requests block short decodes. Prior ticket experiments indicate kernel-selection hints (lightweight probe) and attention-sparsity estimates reduce cost per-token but do not solve cross-tenant starvation at the stage boundary.
problem_statement: We need a scheduling policy that: 1) prevents long prefill ops from indefinitely delaying short, latency-sensitive decodes; 2) preserves high GPU utilization for throughput-oriented tenants; 3) provides predictable latency SLOs for high-tier customers without blowing up unit cost for others; 4) plays nicely with kernel selection and attention optimization signals.
proposal_summary: Implement an elastic reservoir per tenant (or tenant class) maintained by the arbiter. Reservoir tokens are accrued based on historical adherence to SLOs, paid priority (Dedicated vs Hosted), and recent resource consumption. When a prefill is ready to hand off to decode, the arbiter consults reservoir level + attention-cost estimate + kernel-hint probe to pick one of three actions: fast-track (dedicated short-path decode slot), micro-slice (split prefill into N subprefills with scheduled decode windows), or queue-and-batch (delay and merge for high-efficiency kernels). Reservoirs decay on a sliding window to avoid permanent hoarding.
technical_design: Reservoir model: fixed-capacity floating window; tokens earned per successful low-latency responses and purchased via Dedicated commitments; decay half-life configurable per release
Decision inputs: reservoir_level, prefill_length_tokens, attention_sparsity_score, kernel_probe_latency_estimate, tenant_tier, recent_error_rate

Actions: FAST_TRACK (allocate low-latency decode slot + kernel hint to low-latency kernel), MICROSPLIT (split prefill into micro-prefills of configurable max_tokens and schedule progressive decode handoffs), DEFER_BATCH (place into batching pool for throughput kernels), FALLBACK (route to compatible model variant with quantization), HEDGE (duplicate small speculative decode when reservoir insufficient and tenant high-priority)

Kernel integration: arbiter communicates kernel_target_hint (low_latency|high_throughput|quantized) to runtime; kernel probe is a lightweight synthetic latency estimator (per-model, per-device) kept in runtime cache
Metrics and telemetry: per-tenant reservoir level timeseries, handoff action counts, action-specific p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost_per_token_by_action
Safety: hard per-tenant token cap and global soft caps to prevent noisy neighbors; eviction policy for persistent overconsumption
design_decisions: Use per-tenant reservoir with tiers (hosted-free | hosted-paid | dedicated) rather than per-request heuristics to provide predictable behavior
Favor micro-splitting for prefill lengths between 128-2048 tokens where attention-cost variability is highest
Implement kernel_hint enum rather than direct kernel selection so runtime retains final kernel choice based on device availability
Introduce telemetry-first rollout: collect signals in shadow mode for 2 cycles before enabling enforcement
alternatives_considered: Strict priority preemption: simple but causes throughput loss and oscillations
Latency tax charging: charge tokens directly proportional to latency cost; rejected due to complexity in billing integration
Static micro-slicing policy: easier to implement but performs poorly across diverse prompt length distributions
acceptance_criteria: Shadow mode: 2 weeks of shadow runs showing >30% drop in 99p handoff-induced latency for P1 tenants without >5% regression in global throughput
Canary: rollout to 10% of traffic for a single region with no client-facing errors and stable GPU utilization variance within +/-10%
Observability: dashboards showing per-tenant reservoir, action breakdown, and per-action latencies available in Console
Config: operators can tune reservoir decay, micro-slice max size, and action thresholds without code deploy
test_plan: Phase 1 - Simulation: run scheduler simulator with historical trace replays (1 month of mixed traffic) to tune thresholds. Phase 2 - Shadow: enable arbiter decisions in shadow for one production region and record decision outcomes. Phase 3 - Canary: enable enforcement for a small slice of traffic, run load tests with synthetic long-prefill short-decode mixes. Phase 4 - Rollout: staged rollout by tenant tier. Postmortem for any incidents.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge implementation behind feature flag. 2) Start 2-week shadow run (collect telemetry). 3) Canary at 5-10% in us-west1 for 48-72 hours. 4) Expand to 50% if metrics stable. 5) Global enable with operator tuning window. 6) Revisit reservoir parameters after 2 weeks of full load.
monitoring_and_alerts: Create Console alerts: 1) sudden drop in global throughput >15% coincident with handoff action spikes; 2) reservoir depletion rate >5x baseline for any tenant; 3) action_failure_rate >0.5% sustained over 10m
